From: Ted Payne, LANCS.

May I first of all ask for some
advice? I at present own both a
Spectrum 48k (rubber keyboard
version) and a +3, having just
upgraded to the +3, and although
I can programme in BASIC my
machine code knowlege is very
limited, although I do intend
sending for your OUTLET EXTRA 1
as soon as I can afford it which
I am sure will help with m/c but
in the meantime could you help
with the following questions?

1. When using 'old' 48k programs
on the +3 is it possible to make
them save game position to disk
instead of tape. (when running
in 128k mode)?

2. How do you switch 'pages' in
128k mode?
                Ted Payne.



1. You must buy Multiface 3. It
plugs in the back and you just
press a button. It's `35.95(inc.
p&p) from Romantic Robot, 54
Deanscroft Avenue,London,NW9 8EN

2. It is easiest to use the RAM
DISK to get at the extra RAM in
BASIC (p.161 of +3 manual) to
LOAD or MERGE BASIC or images as
needed. If in doubt, let me know
exactly what you want to do. An
example of m/code page-switching
is on p.201 of the +3 manual but
it's not for beginners!
                        - Brian

More SAM bugs from Brian

File copying to the same drive
fails in Mode 1 on DOS 1.3

COPY(may)corrupt disks or it may
be RESET or...

Loading from tape does not force
a scroll if the name falls at
the bottom of the screen as it
does on a Spectrum. Such a load
will fail.

OVER 1 is badly explained. Mode
1 and 2 seem o.k. Mode 4 only
prints PAPER 0;INK 7. Mode 3
does not work correctly at all.

CLS # does not clear the whole
screen of attributes

SCREEN$ (X,Y) does not work in
Mode 3 in some situations.

The BASIC line cursor is printed
in "global" attributes.It should
be in "transparent" colours,e.g.
INK 16 as on a Spectrum. Not
serious- just unprofessional and
unpolished.

A variable file name will SAVE
as BASIC even if CODE or DATA is
specified IF BASIC is over 9K.
E.g., DIM A$(8000):INPUT LINE N$
SAVE N$ CODE 0,50 is o.k.but now
change the 8000 to 9000 and it
crashes.

DOS 1.3 seems to be corrupted by
READ & WRITE (may be just the
same page boundary problem).

DOS 1.3 fails to display multi-
palette SCREEN$ correctly. Tape
loading fails also.

ERASE treats Drive 2 as default
after it has been accessed with
e.g. LOAD "D2:NAME" UNTIL Drive
1 is used to LOAD.

From Dave Scott, CARLISLE

Dear Ron,

Sorry to read about your [SAM]
problems. Like you, I found the
manual confusing.This applies to
all of the literature sent out
by MGT. Their manuals are not a
patch on the original Speccy
manual.

I now have my printer interface
and had trouble getting the
printer to accept CHR$ codes
until, after three phone calls
to MGT,I got someone who advised
using OPEN #3; "B" - yet their
manual states that with a
parallel printer, all that is
necessary is to use LPRINT.

I'm pleased to say that things
are beginning to click [that's
just the drive corrupting yet
another disc - BC] and that I
feel a lot happier with it than
I did a month ago, especially
since Alan Miles tells us we
will be getting the new ROM and
updated DOS about the end of
April and that the guarantee on
our equipment will be for one
year after delivery of the ROM
and DOS.

I must admit that I find the ROM
a real pain as I have very few
games and hundreds of useful
programs, very few of which will
transfer and run. When I try to
adapt them and use the EDIT key,
bringing down say,line 4250 will

actually bring down something
like 3175 and then it locks up.I
can't get it back so the only
thing that I can do according to
MGT is delete it and type back
in the line.

The lack of an INPUT command
that works is also a bit of a
bind and I find the GET command
does not lend itself as a useful
alternative.
                Sincerely,

                  D. Scott

To Dave Scott from Brian


The EDIT problem is caused by
the ROM mishandling the pageing
and occurs in BASIC programs of
over 9K. If you are developing
one section of a larger program
and can split it in two by
deleting half the lines,SAVEing
the remainder, re-LOADing the
original full program, deleting
the other half and SAVEing that
then you should be able to
continue work. Absurd? Yes, it
is absurd - the whole situation
is absurd.

Another way is, when you get the
error,press the BREAK button at
the back right of the machine to


abandon the line in the editor.
Now enter DIM A$(5000) to change
the amount of memory being used
by BASIC. This often works for a
time to let you do a little more
work but results vary. I often
enter the DIM in the first line
of the program.

The problem may arise if the
area of memory which handles the
EDIT (which I assume is just
above BASIC as with a Spectrum)
straddles the page boundary at
32768. Adding the DIM A$(5000)
pushes the EDIT area up to about
37768 and the page boundary now
falls within the (unused) string
array, A$, where it can do no
harm. However, as you continue
to add/delete BASIC lines the


page boundary will move and
cause further problems. I think
sometimes it completely locks up
the edit and then nothing works
- RUN, LIST, etc. and you lose
everything.

This bug's in my Top 5 nightmare
bug list competing with disc
corruption for the No.1 slot.

The INPUT problem can be helped
by using the following...

INPUT LINE I$     or...

INPUT "Enter so and so " LINE A$

      ...for string input. For
numeric input use the same but
add...

       LET I = VAL I$

You may, of course, wish to add
some error-trapping to that.

Neither GET or INKEY$ are direct
substitutes for INPUT but may be
used in a BASIC routine of about
6 or 10 lines to emulate INPUT.

Hope that helps a bit.

                      - Brian

From Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS



Thanks for answering my recent
queries in OUTLETTERS. Whilst I
appreciate the reasons for those
extra CHR$ 13 & 128[in REM lines
in which code is stored] - now!
- I still feel it imposes a
restricton on anyone who wishes
to add extra commands earlier on
in the line.

To Malcolm Goodman from Brian

Firstly, I think you will find
very few lines that would not
cause problems anyway - even if
I remove the 13 and 128.

Secondly- what I think I omitted
from my reply were some methods
I use to get round the problem:-

1. Place a line IN FRONT OF THE
REM LINE and GO SUB that.

2. Do the above but use LINEZIP
(OUTLET 2) to zip the two lines
together into one.

3. Use NEXPIKA (OUTLET 16) to
POKE (very carefully!) a zipped
line with any BASIC you want.

Failing that, the 13 and 128 are
VERY easy to remove by using...

LET NX=PEEK 23637+256*PEEK 23638
: POKE NX+58,32: POKE NX+59,32

    ...in a temporary line just
in front of the REM line.

Nevertheless, I take your final
point that it's just one more
restriction we could do without.

Thanks for the other bits in
your letter, Malcolm,about which
I shall be writing to you direct
if I have not done so already by
the time you read this!
                       - Brian

From M.A. Rodgers, TYNE & WEAR


Is there any way I can change
the control codes in CAL-PLAN
(OUTLET 16) to allow it to work
with +3 Centronics?





Yes, MERGE in the program; add
FORMAT LPRINT "U"at the START of
line 9988; reSAVE the program by
entering RUN 9983;enter RUN 9000
to run CAL-PLAN and select the
"USER" option when you see the
blue printer "sub-menu" prompts.

                       - Brian

Dear Ron,

Since writing last I have (a)
acquired a second-hand SWIFTDISC
(b) finally contacted Ian Hunt
of SIXWORD (0243 771689) (c)had
a helpful phone call from George
Munroe(thanks for passing my
request on!).

Early impressions of SWIFTDISC
have been VERY favourable though
there are a few problems still
to be sorted out mainly to do
with a suitable printer cable
and getting WORDMASTER modified.

The Microdrive Emulation seems
to work very well and could be a
great boon if your fears about
cartridges are corect. However,
I have had some odd (and time-
consuming) experiences. I got
rather complacent when OUTLET 32
A & B transferred easily to disc
and all its contents loaded and
ran O.K. I then transferred 4
cartridges of past OUTLET progs,
only to find that NONE would
load or run, except for the
SCREEN$. I got "file not found",
"out of memory" or a lock-up.
Since than I have found some
other progs OK and others not.

One factor in many but not all,
is progs saved originally with a
Multiface seem not to reload.

Sometime can you publish again
or give me a reminder how best
to save OUTLET progs where there
isn't a save option?.

Ian Hunt says SWIFTDISC is still
available and interest has been
reviving lately (perhaps due to
cartridge shortages) despite the
fact that they don't advertise.
There is also a Users' Group
which I hope to learn more about
if it is still alive. I will let
you know anything more I find
out.

Do you know if there have been
any problems using Citizen 120D
with Spectrums? I may be
replacing my Brother with one.
[Doesn't he mind? -B.C.]

Does INDUG exist? I have had no
reply to my inquiries about SAM.

Issue 31 was very good again.The
Crossword Compiler is enjoyable
to use, even for me.I hope there
will be puzzles published from
time to time and as someone with
no experience in producing or
solving crosswords, some tips on
how best to create them would be
welcome. The page of Clip Art
will be useful and I hope to see
many more in future. Garner
Designs are also now producing
Clip Art, aimed at the Plus 3.

Is there any possibility a low-
cost Scanner may be produced for
the Spectrum? I have the VIDI-ZX
but I would find a scanner much
more useful.    - CHRIS CLAYTON.

To Chris Clayton from Brian

See my reply to L. McKechnie as
to resaving OUTLET programs but
I recommend you contact George
Munroe about transferring to
SWIFTDISC as I believe he has
succeeded with all OUTLET files.
Send details if you contact a
SWIFTDISC user group.

There's no scanner specifically
designed for the Spectrum but
many scanners are available and
I assume they must connect to
other computers via RS232. Does
anyone else have any ideas or
info on this?

The 120D works ok on a Spectrum
and is Epson-compatible.
                        - Brian

From:  J.L. Phillips, DORSET
        (Tel: 0258 880394)



Dear R & B,

Just had my first subscription
issue of OUTLET and already feel
impelled to make a contribution
to your letter pages - on the
subject of the SAM COUPE.

Being an owner of a Coupe (as
well as several Spectrums), and
having experienced similar
troubles to those described by
Richard McGee, Brian Thompson
and (it would seem) many others,
could I start with a plea and a
suggestion..

First, the plea. There must be
many anxiously looking to other
users' experiences to help them
with their own problems so it is
important the equipment being
used is precisely described, for
example, the DOS when discussig
disc problems. Richard McGee's
problems would appear to have
been with Version 1.1 of the DOS
(as first supplied in February).
The current version, as I write,
is Version 1.3. Many of the
problems he describes have been
rectified and other improvements
made and there is the promise of
an upgrade later this month(free
to previous customers) which
should further improve the situ-
ation, including for example,
restoration of the autoload
feature.

Now for my suggestion. This is
that a section of OUTLET should
list names, locality and tele-
phone numbers of Coupe owners so
contacts can be made, locally if
practical, and experiences
shared.


You can start off such a list
with my own details. I have been
through most, if not all, the
problems described in OUTLET 32
and can counsel patience above
all. The problems are recognized
by MGT and are being worked on.
My early depression has now been
replaced by a cautious but, I
believe,a well-founded optimism.

Finally, I must correct the
balance somewhat by putting in a
good word for MGT.Their customer
care section has been very
patient and helpful in dealing
with the problems I have put to
them. They HAVE rung back; they
HAVE cooperated fully with my
suggested "next steps".

I can, like others, reasonably
complain at the unsatisfactory
state of the equipment at launch
but I have no grounds whatsoever
for complaining at the
cooperation of Customer care in
affording assistance and at
minimal cost to myself. (Thanks
Gillian, Sally, Samantha, Andy
and Adrian!)
              Sincerely,
                 Les Phillips.

To Les Phillips from Brian


Many thanks Les. I may well set
up a list as you describe, if
there is a big enough response,
in the new ADD-ENDERS section of
the SAM version of OUTLET. What-
ever happens,however,ALL readers
are, and always have been,
invited to ask for their full
address and/or telephone number
to appear at the top of their
OUTLETTER - and many useful
contacts have been made that
way.
                 - Brian

As a new convert to the magazine
I thought it was about time for
me to submit something (however
large or small). So here it is,
my first (but hopefully not my
last) letter to Outlet. It
contains a few bits'n'bobs which
I hope somebody may find inter-
esting and/or useful.

I am currently using an issue 3
48K Spectrum connected to an
Issue 1 interface 1 and micro-
drive in conjunction with OCSS's
BLAST compiler version 3.7 to
compile BASIC programs. Although

I can compile from tape to tape,
if I select microdrive to tape
or microdrive to microdrive the
program refuses to compile
correctly, crashing when I try
to run it. I would like to get
hold of a newer version of BLAST
just in case the cause of my
problems is a bug in the compil-
er itself.


If anyone can help, a version of
3.8 or above is what I need
(check the loading screen for
version number). Ideally a
version of 4.0 or above (may be
marked as SUPER BLAST+) would be
the best. Please write or phone
me with details.

Help! Problem number 2 concerns
my Spectrum +3. I bought it in
December '88 and had no major
problems until November '89 when
the CPU blew and was subsequent-
ly replaced. Since then the
built-in printer port has
refused to work.


The +3 seems to act normally
when you tell it to print, but
it just doesn't send a signal to
the printer.Even the print test
in the +3's ROM can't get any
response. I have had it in for
repair, but the engineer can't
solve the problem. If anyone can
help please drop me a line and I
will be eternally grateful.

The recent launch of the SAM
Coupe should ensure the Spectrum
spirit lives on well into the
'90's and hopefully beyond.
Having just got hold of one
myself, just a quick couple of
comments on the machine...

Nice styling, decent keyboard,
plenty of ports, fast,high-capa-
city drives, okay tape once you
tune your tape player. Good,
colourful graphics, flexible
sound, high Spectrum compatibil-
ity, powerful BASIC. In short,
BUY ONE!

Just one thing however. There is
a small bug in version 1.2 of
Sam Dos that prevents the Coupe
from recognising drive 2 when

twin drives are fitted. To
correct this load Sam Dos as
usual then type: POKE DVAR 2,208
and then 256K: SAVE "samdos"CODE
229385,10000 or 512K : SAVE
"samdos" CODE 491529,10000
Answer Y to the overwrite file
message, and voila the bug is
fixed.







Many thanks, Thurstan.

                       - Brian

From Ton Voon,

I bought my first Spectrum about
6 years ago. I upgraded to this
beast [PC] in 1987. I used them
mostly for games. However,I went
through a phase of 'how about
doing your own things'. I learnt
BASIC. I was chuffed but that
was it. No further. It would be
too easy to blame the magazines,
mainly because they were good
then - I just lacked determinat-
ion. I regarded machine code the
same way as sex - fasinating but
not enough to go though. Yet.
That's what drew me to Outlet
[What? Sex? - BC](and Format,but
I have fears that they will fall
into the dreaded 'high sales
syndrome' (stay with low sales
forever!)).

With Outlet my Spectrum seems to
have grown more powerful or have
I? 'LET a = VAL"1e4"' Yup, it's
me. It just goes to prove it's
not the machine but the user.

Case in point: I write simple
little programs for my maths
projects (and why not, they
boost my marks), and my friends
look in astonishment. They own
Amigas. They use it to the best
of their abilities - not much.

In fact, I got the SAM Coupe for
wordprocessing, programming and
to 'have a fresh start'.Imagine,
I know the same as everyone
else!But since Outlet, the Coupe
seems unnecessary. Having said
that, the BASIC is definitely
worth having.

Can you tell me whether you get
any sector errors with the disk
(DOS 1.3)? I've been getting
these messages too many times.

If RECORD TO A$ is entered with-
out RECORD STOP then when the
command BLITZ A$ is reached, SAM
NEWS.

DEF KEYCODE 193:: is accepted by
the editor but when you press
the function key, the computer
crashes.

If you delete any invisible INV
marker a ? appears.

PRINT -2!4 [! should be upright
arrow -BC] gives -16. It should
be +16.

OPEN SCREEN n,m,1 doesn't work.

100 ELSE IF T=-1 THEN LET T=1 is
accepted after second press of
RETURN but doesn't work.

FILL x,y,z is accepted but not
issued.

Finally, Outlet Extra is wonder-
ful. I especially love the
Outclass lessons.However,I don't
have enough time to learn m/code
but I'll get to it. Soon. Since
Outclass had memory-saving
techniques, do you have any
BASIC speed efficient routines?

I can hear my maths teacher call
me from the back of my head. I'd
better go. Thanks for listening.
                          - Ton

To Ton Voon from Brian



Thanks Ton. Yes, I got lots of
disk corruption on the SAM too
and must wait for the new ROM
and a properly-working DOS so I
can decide if it's the hardware
or not. My latest thought is it
may be caused when copying but I
have heard it may be when RESET
is pressed with a disc in the
drive.

We had to choose between spend-
ing a few days organising and
appearing at the show or getting
OUTLET ready in time. We thought
about it for 7 seconds which we
suddenly had spare.

The ? shows when you delete INV
or any attribute code because
two bytes are needed, e.g. INK 4
= 16 and 4 and deleting one
leaves an unprintable code which
shows as a ?.Not a major bug but
a lack of polish.The Spectrum is
the same. So are my shoes.

To increase speed AVOID: GO SUBs
[by entering IDENTICAL routines
WHERE THEY ARE NEEDED or put GO
SUBs at the top of a listing
(Spectrum-not SAM)]; "fixed"
variables(like GO TO GETKEY);NOT
PI,VAL "" etc. Cram in each line
as many statements as possible.
The foregoing have drawbacks and
not for general use but ONLY
where YOU judge a program part
to be time-critical.
                       - Brian

From: Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE

What a great program PROCROSS
is! If this is an example of the
sort of software to come I look
forward to future issues and a
possible compilation of the best
of OUTLET.

I was one of those people who
visited "THE ALL-FORMATS SHOW".
What a load of rubbish[gasp!-BC]
I'm sorry but I can't think of
another word for it.Not only did
I have to pay the most I've ever
paid to attend a computer fair
but paid it to see a half-empty
hall! At least they could have
GIVEN you a programme instead of
charging `1 - seeing as a lot of
exhibitors who were advertised
as being there, were not.

Just prior to arriving I was
quite looking forward to seeing
the SAM COUPE and even bringing
one away with me as long as I
got the right answers to
questions I had. The following
will be of interest to FRANK
HARROP (BRIGHTON) and STEVE MONK
(KENT)and other readers.


In mags etc., and by MGT them-
selves, we were promised 80%
software compatability.Well this
really meant games software- not
the sort of software I, and most
other OUTLET readers, use, e.g.,
TASWORD 2, MASTERFILE and LETTA-
HEAD to name jut a few.This type
of program won't work because of
the different DOS SYSTEM set up.

For example you load a game in
and that's it- you just play it.
But in the above software you go
back and forth to disc - that's
where the problem lies and is
what I understood of MGT's
explanation to me at the show.

To put it mildly, I was shatter-
ed! Here was the computer I
thought had good possibilties of
having serious software produced
for it owing to its large memory
(probably will) besides what I
already had; great graphics;nice
drive set up; snapshot facility
etc.; only to find I would not
be able to use any of my serious
software and pay a fortune for
new software.So yes,you guessed,
I didn't take one away with me.

By the way, how nice of MGT to
think of DISCIPLE and +D users
(their words- not mine).They can
supply an i/face to allow us to

To Dave Scott from Brian

The EDIT problem is caused by the ROM mishandling the pageing and occurs in BASIC programs of over 9K. If you are developing one section of a larger program and can split it in two by deleting half the lines,SAVEing the remainder, re-LOADing the original full program, deleting the other half and SAVEing that then you should be able to continue work. Absurd? Yes, it is absurd - the whole situation is absurd.

Another way is, when you get the error,press the BREAK button at the back right of the machine to

abandon the line in the editor. Now enter DIM A$(5000) to change the amount of memory being used by BASIC. This often works for a time to let you do a little more work but results vary. I often enter the DIM in the first line of the program.

The problem may arise if the area of memory which handles the EDIT (which I assume is just above BASIC as with a Spectrum) straddles the page boundary at 32768. Adding the DIM A$(5000) pushes the EDIT area up to about 37768 and the page boundary now falls within the (unused) string array, A$, where it can do no harm. However, as you continue to add/delete BASIC lines the

page boundary will move and cause further problems. I think sometimes it completely locks up the edit and then nothing works - RUN, LIST, etc. and you lose everything.

This bug's in my Top 5 nightmare bug list competing with disc corruption for the No.1 slot.

The INPUT problem can be helped by using the following...

INPUT LINE I$     or...

INPUT "Enter so and so " LINE A$

...for string input. For numeric input use the same but add...

LET I = VAL I$

You may, of course, wish to add some error-trapping to that.

Neither GET or INKEY$ are direct substitutes for INPUT but may be used in a BASIC routine of about 6 or 10 lines to emulate INPUT.

Hope that helps a bit.

- Brian

Если вы разрабатываете одну часть большой программы и можете разделить ее на две, удалив половину строк, сохранив (SAVE) остаток, повторно загрузив (LOAD) исходную полную программу, удалив другую половину и сохранив ее — тогда вы сможете продолжить работу. Другой способ: когда возникает ошибка, нажмите кнопку BREAK в задней правой части машины, чтобы выйти из строки в редакторе. Теперь введите DIM A$(5000), чтобы изменить объем памяти, используемой BASIC. Это часто работает некоторое время, чтобы дать вам возможность сделать еще немного работы, но результаты варьируются. Добавление DIM A$(5000) сдвигает область EDIT примерно до 37768, и граница страницы теперь попадает в (неиспользуемый) массив строк A$, где она не может причинить вреда.
